title: Iran's Khamenei urges Gulf rulers in written message to confront 'real enemy'
gist: In a written Islamic Unity Week message, Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei urged Gulf and Muslim countries to unite against a 'real enemy' and cited Palestinian helplessness as the cost of disunity, his first notable outreach since being injured in US-Israeli airstrikes six months ago that killed his father and predecessor Ali Khamenei and launched the Iran war.

themes.theme: Khamenei's unity appeal to the Gulf

insights.claim: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei urged Muslim countries, particularly those in the Gulf, to unite against what he called their 'real enemy' in a message published on his Telegram account for Islamic Unity Week.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The new Iranian leader's direct appeal to Gulf monarchies is a diplomatic signal to watch for any thaw or realignment amid the ongoing Iran war.
insights.quote: identify your real enemy, understand his plan and confront it
insights.locator: My emphatic and repeated recommendation to the rulers

insights.claim: Khamenei asked whether Palestinians would have been left 'so helpless' if Muslims had been united, and said anyone who creates divisions among Muslims, knowingly or unknowingly, helps Islam's enemies.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Invoking Palestinian suffering to press Muslim unity is Tehran's framing device to rally the region against Israel and the US.
insights.locator: It asked whether Palestinians would have been left

insights.claim: Khamenei specifically asked Gulf Arab rulers whether 'rogues without identity' would have dared to covet their lands and possessions had the Gulf's peoples and governments been united under the flag of Islam.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Framing external actors as threats to Gulf territory is an appeal to shared security fears, a rhetorical pivot from Iran's historic rivalry with the monarchies.
insights.locator: Khamenei specifically asked Gulf Arab rulers

themes.theme: Leadership transition and the Iran war

insights.claim: Mojtaba Khamenei has not been seen in public since being injured in US-Israeli airstrikes six months ago that launched the Iran war and killed his father and previous supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A wounded, publicly absent new supreme leader who inherited power via his father's killing signals fragility at the top of the Iranian state.
insights.locator: Khamenei has not been seen in public

insights.claim: Khamenei's unity call echoes a Friday statement to Iranians in which he said he had banned actions that harm social cohesion and urged authorities to avoid 'discouraging statements' that weaken national and public morale.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Domestic messaging policing morale and cohesion suggests internal strain within Iran that could affect regime stability.
insights.locator: His call for unity echoes a statement he made on Friday

insights.claim: During the present conflict Tehran has struck US military facilities and other infrastructure in Gulf states, underscoring tensions between Iran and its Gulf neighbours despite the unity appeal.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Iran attacking Gulf infrastructure while calling for unity exposes the contradiction limiting any genuine rapprochement, keeping Gulf risk premia elevated.
insights.locator: During the present conflict, Tehran has struck U.S. military

insights.claim: Since the 1979 Islamic Revolution, Gulf Arab monarchies have viewed Iran's revolutionary ideology, anti-monarchic rhetoric and regional influence as a threat to their political systems.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The long-standing monarchic distrust of Iran's ideology is the structural barrier that makes Khamenei's unity pitch a hard sell.
insights.locator: Since the 1979 Islamic Revolution, Gulf Arab monarchies
